name: The Grand Exchange

stars.name: Exchange Primary
stars.notes: Bright F-type primary, high luminosity provides energy abundance for the system's massive industrial and commercial operations.

stars.name: Exchange Secondary
stars.notes: Cooler companion in a wide orbit, its habitable zone hosts the system's most Earth-like world.

planets.name: Ingot
planets.notes: Superheated metallic world orbiting Exchange Primary. Extremely rich in heavy metals but too hostile for conventional mining.

planets.name: Auction
planets.notes: Super-Earth trade capital orbiting Exchange Primary, population 5.8 billion. Its higher gravity has produced a stocky, resilient human phenotype adapted to the world's 1.3g pull.

planets.name: Consignment
planets.notes: Dry world with thin atmosphere, heavily industrialized for manufacturing and warehousing. Population 120 million, mostly transient workers.

planets.name: Yield
planets.notes: Dominant gas giant in the primary star's outer system. Fuel harvesting megastructures orbit permanently within its upper atmosphere.

planets.name: Emporium
planets.notes: Ocean world orbiting Exchange Secondary, population 2.1 billion. Floating city-platforms host the system's cultural and diplomatic centers.

planets.name: Commodity
planets.notes: Cold, airless world orbiting Exchange Secondary. Automated mining extracts rare isotopes from deep impact craters.

planets.name: Reserve
planets.notes: Ice giant in the secondary star's outer system. Several moons host research outposts studying its unusual magnetic field.

planets.name: Futures
planets.notes: Distant frozen world at the system's edge. Long-term terraforming proposals have been debated for decades without resolution.

anomalies.name: The Bid-Ask Shimmer
anomalies.notes: Persistent electromagnetic distortion in the space between the binary pair. Ships transiting the zone report instrument fluctuations and brief communication blackouts.

asteroid_belts.name: The Margin Call
asteroid_belts.location: Between orbits 3 and 4 around Exchange Primary
asteroid_belts.notes: Extremely rich asteroid belt that has been under continuous mining for over two centuries. Major source of raw materials for the system's manufacturing sector.

stations.name: The Floor
stations.notes: The largest trading station in the Cygnus Commercial Belt. Its name derives from the original trading floor where commodities futures were physically exchanged.

stations.name: Clearinghouse
stations.notes: Financial services and cargo certification hub. Houses the Exchange Banking Authority and seventeen licensed insurance underwriters.

stations.name: Emporium Gateway
stations.notes: Primary trade station for the secondary star's planets. Specializes in luxury goods, cultural artifacts, and diplomatic services.

stations.name: The Mint
stations.location: Lagrange point between the two stars
stations.notes: Heavily fortified financial data center and currency exchange. Processes interstellar credit transfers for the entire sector.

faction_control.notes: Powerful mercantile oligarchy that controls the system through economic leverage rather than military force. Member corporations hold seats on the Directorate in proportion to their trade volume.

history: The Grand Exchange was established in 2267 as a deliberate commercial venture by a consortium of megacorporations seeking a neutral trading ground beyond the jurisdiction of any single faction government.

The discovery of The Margin Call asteroid belt's extraordinary mineral wealth in 2312 transformed the system from a trading post into an industrial powerhouse, funding the construction of the massive station infrastructure that defines it today.

The Exchange Directorate weathered the Cygnus Recession of 2534 by opening its markets to smaller independent traders, a pragmatic decision that paradoxically strengthened the system by diversifying its commercial base.
description: The Grand Exchange is commerce made manifest, a binary star system engineered from its earliest settlement to serve as the sector's premier marketplace. Exchange Primary's bright yellow-white light illuminates Auction, a super-Earth trade capital where 5.8 billion people participate in an economy so vast it sets commodity prices for dozens of surrounding systems. Across the stellar divide, Exchange Secondary's gentler orange glow falls on Emporium, an ocean world whose floating cities provide the cultural and diplomatic counterweight to Auction's relentless mercantilism. Eight worlds in total orbit the paired stars, nearly all bent to the service of trade.

The system's infrastructure is staggering in scale. The Floor, orbiting Auction, is one of the largest stations in known space, its two million inhabitants processing cargo volumes that defy easy comprehension. The Clearinghouse handles the financial architecture, the Emporium Gateway manages the luxury trade, and The Mint, hanging at the gravitational balance point between the stars, processes credit transfers for the entire Cygnus Commercial Belt. The Margin Call asteroid belt has been mined for two centuries and shows no signs of exhaustion, feeding raw materials into manufacturing operations on Consignment that supply half the sector.

For all its commercial supremacy, The Grand Exchange operates under tensions that its Directorate works hard to conceal. The Bid-Ask Shimmer between the binary stars disrupts communications in ways that physicists cannot fully explain, and some theorists argue it is slowly intensifying. The Directorate's corporate oligarchy faces growing pressure from independent traders who were welcomed during the recession but now demand political representation proportional to their economic contribution. And deep in The Mint's encrypted archives, there are records that even Directorate members cannot access, sealed since the system's founding and subject to security protocols that predate every current institution.
